Apple Unveils First MacBook Pro with a Touchscreen and OLED Display

On October 28, 2026, at its "Pro and Tell" event in Los Angeles, Apple announced new MacBook Pro models featuring a PROLED XDR display. These are the first Mac laptops to support touch input and utilize a tandem OLED screen. The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 (with the M5 Pro chip), while the 16-inch model begins at $3,399 (also with the M5 Pro). Configurations featuring the M5 Max chip start at $4,499 and $4,799, respectively. Pre-orders open on October 28, with shipments beginning November 6.

The display offers brightness of up to 2,000 nits (for both HDR and SDR content), a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1, and an adaptive refresh rate ranging from 10 Hz to 120 Hz (ProMotion). The touch sensor is integrated directly into the display panel. New features include the "Dynamic Island," an illuminated Apple logo on the lid, and a lighter chassis (the 14-inch model weighs approximately 1.36 kg). The devices are powered by the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips found in previous models, supporting up to 128 GB of RAM and up to 16 TB of storage. They are available in Space Black and Silver, with an optional nano-texture glass finish.

In the days leading up to the event, Apple also introduced an updated iPad mini (8th generation), featuring an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, a thinner 5.4 mm chassis, IP67-rated protection, and a new speaker system. The starting price is $699 (for the Wi-Fi model with 128 GB of storage). In addition, a 14-inch MacBook Pro and an iMac powered by the M6 ​​chip were announced (with starting prices of $1,999 and $1,499, respectively). These devices will go on sale during the same timeframe.

📌 Governance Snapshots: Why Your Tokens May Not Count in a DAO Vote

Main Points
⏺ Some DAOs calculate voting power using token balances from a specific blockchain block
⏺ Buying tokens after that snapshot may not increase your voting power
⏺ This post explains how balance snapshots work and why purchase timing matters

1️⃣ Core Idea — the protocol records balances at a selected block to determine how many votes each participant receives.
2️⃣ Why It Exists — a fixed reference point prevents voting power from changing every time tokens are transferred during the voting process.
3️⃣ Example — a vote uses balances from block #1000, but you buy tokens at block #1005. Those new tokens won't increase your voting power for that proposal.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — users may buy governance tokens specifically to participate, only to discover the snapshot already happened.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before buying governance tokens, check the snapshot block, delegation conditions, and voting eligibility rules.

Final Thoughts

DAO governance isn't only about how many tokens you hold. It can also depend on when you held them. Sometimes your voting power is decided before the vote even begins.

Ukraine Waits as Hegseth Delays Critical Patriot Missiles


Ukraine has been waiting nearly a month for U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to approve the transfer of critical air defense missiles, Zelensky said Monday, warning that delays could put more lives at risk.

“We have been waiting for nearly a month for Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS,” Zelensky wrote on social media, adding that Kyiv would raise the issue with Washington again while pursuing talks with other countries.

Although the United States has continued providing some military assistance, the Pentagon has yet to complete the required approval process for certain Patriot interceptor transfers from allied countries. 

According to The Kyiv Independent, the pending shipment is significant. Patriot missiles are essential to Ukraine’s defense against Russian ballistic missiles, drones and other aerial attacks. With supplies running critically low, delays threaten Kyiv’s ability to protect cities and vital energy infrastructure from Moscow’s continued bombardment.

Hegseth has said Washington’s policy toward Ukraine has not changed, emphasizing that the United States must ensure its own forces have sufficient interceptors. Zelensky, however, urged Washington to accelerate decisions already under consideration, stressing that every weapons shipment could help save lives.

Ukraine is also facing challenges linked to disruptions affecting Starlink services used by its forces, while Zelensky said Kyiv received no advance warning of several Russian ballistic missile attacks last week. 

The United States maintains that its intelligence-sharing arrangements with Ukraine have not changed.

🌐 Tron founder Justin Sun has accumulated nearly 3% of PEPE’s supply, with blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identifying approximately $51.25 million worth of the memecoin across his known and suspected wallets. According to an October 27 Arkham Intelligence report, the tokens entered Sun-linked wallets over the previous 10 days, making him the largest individual PEPE holder outside cryptocurrency exchanges.

🔗 The firm estimated his combined holdings at 2.82% of PEPE’s supply, although some wallets included in its calculations were attributed to Sun through blockchain analysis. At the time, PEPE had a market capitalization of approximately $1.81 billion, with exchanges controlling several of the largest known holdings.

📊 Binance held $337.5 million worth of PEPE, representing 18.7% of the supply, followed by Robinhood with $150.9 million, or 8.37%. Coinbase and OKX accounted for another 5.03% and 4.15%, respectively. Unlike Sun’s attributed holdings, exchange balances generally include assets held on behalf of customers, meaning their large positions do not necessarily represent investments made by the platforms themselves.
